label: PlanReady
payload:
Implementation Plan: Standard-Monthly Revenue Calculation & Reporting

1) Summary/Goal
- Add a deterministic monthly revenue calculation and reporting pipeline that aggregates invoice/transaction data to produce a monthly revenue report and API endpoint + UI view. Complexity: MEDIUM (no breaking schema changes expected).

2) Scope & Assumptions
- Inputs: existing transactions/invoices table(s).
- No incompatible DB schema changes; use additive columns/tables and backfill where necessary.
- Backwards-compatible API; rollout behind a feature flag.

3) Deliverables
- Calculation service/module implementing monthly aggregation (unit-tested).
- Scheduled job (cron) to run monthly; idempotent and resumable.
- API endpoint returning monthly revenue and metadata.
- UI report page with pagination/filter by month.
- Backfill script for historical months (safe, rate-limited).
- Monitoring dashboards and alerts (processing failures, data drift).

4) Tasks (high-level, assign to Implementer)
- Design (data model, query plan, edge cases) — 1 day
- Implement aggregation logic + unit tests — 2 days
- Add idempotent scheduled job + integration tests — 1 day
- API endpoint + contract tests — 1 day
- UI report + e2e tests — 2 days
- Backfill script + dry-run verification — 1 day
- Observability: metrics, logs, alerts — 0.5 day
- Documentation & rollout plan (feature flag, migration notes) — 0.5 day
Estimated total: ~9 days of engineering effort (can be parallelized).

5) Tests
- Unit tests: calculation correctness, edge cases (returns/refunds, timezone, partial months).
- Integration tests: job scheduling, DB interactions, idempotency.
- Contract tests: API stability and response schema.
- E2E tests (BrowserTester): UI displays correct totals for seeded test data; error states.
- Performance test: aggregation on production-like dataset to ensure runtime and memory bounds.

6) Rollout & Rollback Strategy
- Feature-flagged rollout (disabled by default). Enable for shadow mode first (compute and compare but don’t expose). If results match expectations, enable for subset of users/tenants, monitor.
- DB changes: additive only; any schema migration is backward compatible and reversible if minimal (drop column only when safe).
- Backfill: run in dry-run mode, then incrementally; if issues found, stop and re-run with corrected logic.
- Rollback: disable feature flag (immediate), revert service deployment if necessary, run compensating job to restore previous state if a data mutation was unsafe.

7) Monitoring & Alerts
- Alert on job failures, significant reconciliation diffs between new and canonical revenue, high-latency queries, and increased error rates on API/UI.

8) Post-deploy Verification
- Nightly reconciliation report for first 30 days comparing historical revenue to prior system; manual sign-off.

9) Risks & Mitigations
- Risk: edge-case transactions (refunds, adjustments) miscounted. Mitigate: include comprehensive unit tests and reconciliation step.
- Risk: long-running aggregation. Mitigate: incremental windowed aggregation and limits.

10) Next Steps for Orchestrator
- If you confirm complexity MEDIUM, proceed to Reviewer only; if you judge HIGH (requires Critic), request Critic involvement.

payload:
Replan: Fixes for E2E Failures (checkout_flow_spec payment mock timeouts; order_summary_spec rounding mismatch)

1) Objectives
- Stabilize payment gateway mock to eliminate intermittent timeouts in E2E tests.
- Make price formatter deterministic (fixed rounding rules) and ensure all codepaths use it.
- Add focused integration and E2E tests covering gateway retries/timeouts and rounding edge-cases.
- Assess and, if required, provide a safe backfill/compensating migration for any persisted rounding drift.

2) Work Items & Implementation Details
A. Payment Gateway Mock Stability (owner: Implementer)
- Increase default mock timeout and add configurable retry/backoff in the test harness (e.g., from 2s to 10s, with 3 retry attempts for transient failures).
- Harden the mock to deterministically simulate success/failure modes via fixture flags so tests don’t rely on timing.
- Add integration test that intentionally simulates brief gateway slowness to validate retry behaviour.
- Add logging/metrics in test runs to capture gateway latency and failure rates.

B. Deterministic Rounding Fix (owner: Implementer)
- Centralize price formatting/rounding into a single utility with explicit rounding policy (bankers vs. half-up — choose half-up if business requirement, or confirm otherwise).
- Replace ad-hoc formatters across codebase to use the utility; add comprehensive unit tests covering boundaries (0.005, 0.0049, negative prices, refunds, cumulative sums).
- Audit codepaths that persist rounded values vs. compute display-only rounding and standardize behavior: prefer storing precise decimals (e.g., cents as integer or decimal with scale) and rounding only for display unless business requires persisted rounded totals.

C. Tests to Add (owner: QA/BrowserTester + Implementer)
- E2E: checkout_flow_spec — new scenarios: (1) gateway slow response with eventual success, (2) gateway transient failure + retry success, (3) gateway hard failure path.
- E2E: order_summary_spec — scenarios with prices that hit rounding boundaries and aggregated orders to verify totals match expected deterministic rounding.
- Integration: job-level tests for any services that aggregate persisted prices to ensure no cumulative rounding drift.
- Unit: formatter unit tests with exhaustive edge-case table-driven tests.

D. Backfill / Data Migration Assessment & Strategy (owner: Implementer + Planner)
- Run a conservative audit script (dry-run) that compares current persisted totals vs. recalculated totals using the new deterministic rounding rules across a sample of recent orders (e.g., last 90 days) to quantify delta and potential impact.
- If deltas are non-zero and business requires persisted correction, plan an incremental backfill with safe, idempotent updates and reconciliation: (1) dry-run; (2) small-batch apply with verification; (3) full-run with monitoring; (4) provide compensating entries or adjustments if necessary.
- If persisted values should remain canonical (business decision), avoid automatic backfill and instead surface reconciliation reports for manual resolution.

3) Rollout & Safety
- Apply fixes behind CI-only feature flags where possible; run full test suite in CI before merging to main branch.
- Run the dry-run audit in staging against a recent DB snapshot before any production backfill.
- If backfill needed, execute during low-traffic windows with monitoring and a rollback plan (ability to re-run with prior values or to disable corrective job).

4) Estimates & Timeline (parallelizable)
- Payment gateway mock stability: 0.5–1.0 day (implementation + integration test)
- Deterministic rounding utility & code audit: 0.5–1.0 day (implementation + unit tests)
- Targeted integration & E2E tests: 0.5–1.0 day
- Backfill audit script & dry-run analysis: 0.5 day
- Backfill implementation (only if required by audit): 0.5–1.5 day (depends on scope of deltas)
Estimated total (without backfill): ~2.0–3.0 days; with backfill (if required): ~2.5–4.5 days.

5) Deliverables
- Updated test harness with gateway retry/timeouts and deterministic mock flags.
- Centralized price formatter utility and migration of callers.
- New unit/integration/E2E tests for the fixed scenarios.
- Audit report from dry-run backfill analysis and backfill script if required.

6) Next Steps for Orchestrator
- Approve this replan (estimates and strategy). If approved, I will hand off to Implementer to implement fixes, and QA/BrowserTester to run the newly targeted E2E tests; if the audit requires backfill, confirm whether automated correction is authorized or whether manual reconciliation is preferred.

Plan: Update billing rate calculation to new tariff rules (MEDIUM complexity)

Overview:
- Implement new tariff-rule logic in the billing rate calculation, update config, and add tests and e2e validation. No DB schema changes expected.

Goals:
- Correctly apply new tariff rules to all billing calculations.
- Preserve backwards compatibility for unaffected flows; provide a rollback path.

Scope / Files to modify:
- src/billing/RateCalculator.java (core calculation logic)
- src/config/TariffConfig.yaml (new rules + parser update)
- src/services/BillingService.java (integration glue / rounding/edge cases)
- src/controllers/BillingController.java (if any API contract adjustments required)
- test/unit/billing/RateCalculatorTest.java (unit tests)
- test/integration/EndToEndBillingTest.java (integration test covering common scenarios)
- test/e2e/billing_flow_spec.js (browser/e2e billing flow)
- docs/CHANGELOG.md and docs/README_TARIFF.md (explain behavior)

1) Add/extend TariffConfig model and parser to represent new rule set; add sample YAML entries.
2) Implement new rule evaluation in RateCalculator with clear feature-flag toggle (config flag) to switch new logic on/off.
3) Add unit tests covering each tariff rule case and edge cases (boundary times, zero/negative amounts, precision/rounding).
4) Update BillingService integration points to consume new calculation and ensure rounding/aggregation matches expectations.
5) Update/extend integration tests to include representative customer scenarios and invoicing flow.
6) Add e2e test(s) validating a full billing flow (create usage, run billing job, verify invoice amounts) in test/e2e.
7) Run static analysis, linters, and update docs/CHANGELOG.md.
8) Peer review & merge; deploy behind feature flag to staging and run full e2e suite; monitor metrics; then promote to production.
9) Provide rollback plan: flip feature-flag off or revert merge/patch release if major regression.

- All unit tests pass; coverage maintained for modified modules.
- Integration tests pass in CI.
- Staging e2e billing flow passes and spot-checks against legacy calculator for a sample set.
- No API contract changes visible to clients; if present, document and version appropriately.

- Implementation + unit tests: 1.5 - 2 dev days (12-16 hours).
- Integration tests, e2e, review & staging validation: 0.5 - 1 dev day (4-8 hours).
- Total: 2 - 3 dev days.

Risks & Mitigations:
- Risk: rounding/precision differences -> mitigation: add deterministic rounding utility and tests. 
- Risk: missed edge tariff combination -> mitigation: matrix of tariff cases in unit tests and a sampling in e2e.

- Updated code and config, unit + integration + e2e tests, updated docs, deployment to staging behind feature flag, and production promotion once tests & review are green.
